title: How modern life is increasing stress—and what science says about it
titleZh: 深呼吸、运动、断联：科学教你缓解压力
summary:
过去二十年，科技发展的速度早已超越了人类自身的进化节奏。我们从座机时代迈入全天候在线的数字生活，但我们大脑所依赖的，却依然是那套为远古生存而设计的古老“硬件”。这种“速度落差”，正是我们长期感到不堪重负的根源。我们的祖先只需应对真实猛兽带来的短暂冲击，而今天，我们面对的却是全天持续不断的“微型警报”。一封措辞强硬的邮件，一条社交媒体通知，都可能引发与遭遇猛兽时类似的心跳加速。我们的身体无法分辨这究竟是一个数字弹窗，还是一次真实的生存威胁。因此，在2026年的今天感到压力重重，并不是你个人的问题；这只是你作为一个生命体，对这个永不停歇的世界所产生的自然生理反应。

来源：伦敦每日新闻网；作者：Hassan Javed；原文发布时间：2026-02-24 20:08:00

paragraphs.contentEn: In the last twenty years, technology has outpaced human evolution. We have traded landlines for 24/7 digital expectations, yet our brains still use ancient “hardware” designed for survival. This “speed gap” explains why we feel constantly overwhelmed. Our ancestors faced short bursts of stress from physical predators, but today, we face “small alarms” all day. An angry email or a social media notification triggers the same heart-racing response as a literal lion. Your body cannot distinguish between a digital ping and a physical threat. Being stressed in 2026 isn’t a personal flaw; it’s a natural biological reaction to a world that never stops.
paragraphs.contentZh: 过去二十年，科技发展的速度早已超越了人类自身的进化节奏。我们从座机时代迈入全天候在线的数字生活，但我们大脑所依赖的，却依然是那套为远古生存而设计的古老“硬件”。这种“速度落差”，正是我们长期感到不堪重负的根源。我们的祖先只需应对真实猛兽带来的短暂冲击，而今天，我们面对的却是全天持续不断的“微型警报”。一封措辞强硬的邮件，一条社交媒体通知，都可能引发与遭遇猛兽时类似的心跳加速。我们的身体无法分辨这究竟是一个数字弹窗，还是一次真实的生存威胁。因此，在2026年的今天感到压力重重，并不是你个人的问题；这只是你作为一个生命体，对这个永不停歇的世界所产生的自然生理反应。

paragraphs.contentEn: When your phone pings, your brain’s alarm system—the amygdala—triggers a release of cortisol and adrenaline. While these chemicals were meant for short-term survival, modern life keeps us in this “high alert” mode for hours. This prevents the body from entering the essential “rest and digest” state needed for long-term health, leaving us feeling permanently “fried.” Much of this mental exhaustion stems from “decision overload.” We make thousands of choices daily, which drains the brain’s energy. To combat this, experts recommend using self-exploration questions to filter the noise. Asking, “Is this notification worth my peace of mind?” helps narrow your focus. By making fewer, more intentional decisions, you protect your mental battery and save your precious energy for the things that truly matter.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当手机提示音响起，大脑的警报系统——杏仁核——会被激活，促使身体释放皮质醇和肾上腺素。这些激素原本用于应对短期生存威胁，但在现代生活中，我们往往会连续数小时处于这种“高度警觉”状态。长此以往，身体难以进入维持健康所必需的“休息与消化”模式，人也因此常感到持续性的“精疲力竭”。这种心理耗竭，很大程度上源于“决策过载”。人们每天都要做出成千上万次选择，而每一次决定都在消耗大脑的能量。为此，专家建议通过内省式提问来筛除干扰。比如问自己：“这条通知，真的值得打断我的内心平静吗？”这样的提问有助于收束注意力的范围。当我们减少决策次数，转而做出更有意识、更有取舍的选择时，就能为大脑节省更多心智能量，将宝贵的精力专注在真正重要的事情上。

paragraphs.contentEn: Beyond our screens, the physical world around us is also contributing to our stress levels. Urban life is full of sensory overload. The constant hum of traffic, the bright glare of artificial lights, and the feeling of being in crowded spaces keep our nervous systems on edge. This is especially true at night; the “blue light” from our devices tricks our brains into thinking it is still daytime, which ruins our sleep. When we don’t sleep, our ability to handle stress the next day disappears, creating a vicious cycle of fatigue.
paragraphs.contentZh: 放下电子设备，我们身处的现实世界同样在推高压力水平。城市生活本身就充满感官负荷。持续不断的交通噪音、刺眼的人工照明，以及身处拥挤空间时产生的压迫感，都会让神经系统难以松弛。这种影响在夜间尤为致命；电子屏幕发出的“蓝光”会干扰大脑的判断，使其误以为仍处于白天，从而打乱正常的睡眠节律。而一旦睡眠不足，第二天应对压力的能力便会明显下降，疲劳由此累积，形成难以摆脱的恶性循环。

paragraphs.contentEn: There is also a “loneliness paradox” happening today. We are more digitally connected than ever, but our bodies don’t recognise a text message as true social support. From a scientific perspective, humans need physical presence—eye contact, a handshake, or a shared meal—to feel safe. Without these real-world connections, our bodies feel “biologically lonely,” which the brain interprets as a survival threat. We are realising that the 24/7 lifestyle has messed with our natural biological clocks, leading to a constant feeling of being rushed and alone.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如今，一种“孤独悖论”正日益显现。我们在数字世界中的联系前所未有地紧密，但身体却不会将一条消息视为真正的社会支持。从科学角度看，人类需要真实的身体在场——眼神交汇、一次握手，或是同桌共饮——来建立安全感。缺少这些现实互动时，身体会陷入一种“生理性的孤独”状态，而大脑则可能将这种状态解读为潜在的生存威胁。人们逐渐意识到，全天候在线的生活方式已经扰乱了我们的自然生物节律，导致我们总在赶路，却始终孤独。

paragraphs.contentEn: The good news is that science shows we aren’t stuck this way. The brain has a quality called “neuroplasticity,” which means it can change and adapt. Even if you have been stressed for years, you can “retrain” your brain to be calmer. One of the most effective ways to do this is by understanding the “gut-brain connection.” Scientists have found that the way we breathe and the health of our digestive system send direct signals to the brain. Taking slow, deep breaths tells your brain that there is no immediate danger, allowing your alarm system to turn off.
paragraphs.contentZh: 好消息是，科学研究表明，我们并不是只能被动困在这种状态里。大脑具备一种被称为“神经可塑性”的特质，也就是说，它可以发生改变并不断适应。即便长期承受压力，人们依然可以通过“重新训练”大脑，让自己变得更加平静。实现这一点的有效方式之一，是理解“肠脑连接”。科学家发现，我们的呼吸方式以及消化系统的健康状态，都会向大脑传递直接信号。当我们进行缓慢而深长的呼吸时，大脑会接收到当前没有紧急危险的信息，从而促使警报系统逐步平静下来。

paragraphs.contentEn: We are also learning about the healing power of nature, often called “Biophilia.” Research shows that even a short walk in a park—or just looking at a picture of a forest—can lower your heart rate and blood pressure almost instantly. Nature acts like a “reset button” for your nervous system. It provides the quiet and the “soft focus” that our brains crave after hours of staring at sharp, bright screens. By spending even ten minutes outside, you are giving your brain the signal it needs to stand down from its high-alert status.
paragraphs.contentZh: 与此同时，人们也逐渐认识到大自然所蕴含的疗愈力量，这一概念常被称为“亲生命性”（Biophilia）。研究显示，即便只是在公园里短暂散步，或仅仅是观看一张森林的图片，也能在短时间内降低心率和血压。大自然就像是神经系统的“重置键”。在长时间暴露于刺眼明亮的电子屏幕后，大脑会本能地渴求自然环境所提供的宁静，以及那种“柔和舒展的视觉体验”。哪怕每天只在户外待上十分钟，也是在向大脑发出信号：警报解除，可以休息了。

paragraphs.contentEn: You don’t need a month-long vacation to fix your stress; science suggests that “micro-breaks” are actually more effective. Taking just one minute to breathe deeply several times a day can prevent your cortisol levels from climbing too high. Think of it as a pressure-release valve for your mind. Instead of waiting until you are completely burnt out, you are managing the pressure as it builds.
paragraphs.contentZh: 缓解压力并不必然依赖一次为期一月的假期；科学研究表明，短而频繁的“微休息”反而更为有效。每天多次花上一分钟进行深呼吸，可以防止体内皮质醇水平持续升高。可以将这种做法想象成为大脑安装了一个“减压阀”。与其等到身心彻底枯竭才试图补救，不如在压力逐渐累积的过程中就及时释放。

paragraphs.contentEn: Another vital step is building “quiet zones” in your life. This could mean a rule where phones aren’t allowed at the dinner table or a “digital sunset” where all screens go off an hour before bed. These boundaries aren’t just about productivity; they are about biology. Your brain needs periods of “unreachability” to repair itself. Finally, don’t forget the power of movement. Simple exercise, like a brisk walk or stretching, helps “burn off” the extra adrenaline and cortisol that build up when you’re stressed. Movement tells your body that the “fight” is over, and it’s time to relax.
paragraphs.contentZh: 另一个关键步骤，是在生活中主动设立“安静区”。这可以是规定餐桌上不许出现手机，也可以是实行“数字宵禁”，即在睡前一小时关闭所有电子屏幕。这些界限并不仅仅关乎效率；而是出于生理需要。大脑需要一段“不被连通”的时间，才能完成自我修复。此外，也不要忽视运动的作用。简单的身体活动，例如快走或拉伸，可以帮助“消耗”在压力状态下累积的肾上腺素和皮质醇。当身体开始运动时，它会接收到一个信号：“紧张状态”已经结束，可以逐渐放松下来。

paragraphs.contentEn: Modern life is designed for machines, but we are still very much human. We cannot change the fact that the world is moving fast, and we cannot delete all technology. However, we can learn how to protect our “human side” from the rush. Understanding that your stress is a biological response—not a personal weakness—is the first step toward feeling better. The big takeaway is that you have the power to influence your own nervous system. By choosing to breathe, to move, and to disconnect for a few minutes each day, you are choosing health over haste. You are designing a life that respects your biological limits. When you take care of the human inside, the fast-paced world outside starts to feel a lot less threatening.
paragraphs.contentZh: 现代生活的节奏更适合机器运转，但我们始终是人类。世界狂奔不停，我们无法改变，科技如影随形，我们无法删除。然而，我们可以学会在这种高速节奏中，守护自己的“人类属性”。理解压力是一种生理反应——而不是个人缺陷——是改善状态的第一步。最重要的是，你有能力影响自己的神经系统。每天花几分钟去呼吸、去运动、去暂时与外界断开连接，其实是在主动选择健康，而不是被匆忙裹挟。这意味着，你正在为自己建立一种尊重生理节律的生活方式。当内在的神经系统得到照顾，外部高速运转的世界，也就不再显得那么具有威胁性。
